questions.q: Match each social engineering technique to what it involves.
pairs: Inventing a story to persuade someone to hand over information
Watching someone enter a password or PIN
Leaving infected media where somebody will pick it up
Redirecting a user to a fake website without them noticing
questions.feedback: All four exploit people rather than software, which is why no amount of anti-malware stops them.
questions.revisitLabel: 1.4 Lesson 5 — Social engineering HQ, station 2: Blagging

questions.q: Explain why people are often described as the weakest point in a computer system's security.

markPoints.concept: people can be tricked into giving away information or access
markPoints.exemplar: People can be tricked into giving away their password.

markPoints.concept: and no amount of technical protection prevents that
accept: no technical|no firewall|no amount of|no software|no encryption|cannot stop|cannot prevent|will not stop|does not stop|no safeguard|no defence|nothing technical|bypass|gets round|goes round
markPoints.exemplar: No firewall or encryption can prevent somebody simply telling an attacker their password.

questions.example: People can be persuaded, frightened or flattered into handing over a password or letting someone through a door, and no firewall, encryption or anti-malware prevents that — the attacker has gone round the technology rather than through it.
questions.paraphrase: Staff can be deceived into revealing credentials or granting access, and no technical safeguard can stop somebody who simply tells an attacker what they want to know.
questions.feedback: Tricked, and then why the technology does not help.
